title: Sean Penn, Ava DuVernay and Laura Poitras Turn Out For San Francisco’s Doc Stories
description: Sean Penn isn’t exactly a fixture on the regional documentary festival circuit. But SFFILM’s Doc Stories has a way of attracting high-profile suppo
body:
Sean Penn isn’t exactly a fixture on the regional documentary festival circuit. But SFFILM’s Doc Stories has a way of attracting high-profile supporters.

	On Saturday, Penn was at the fest’s Vogue Theatre in San Francisco to introduce James Marcus Haney’s “Black Sunflowers,” a documentary about a generation of young Ukrainians coming of age amid martial law and the demands of a country at war. Penn, an outspoken supporter of Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, signed on as the film’s executive producer before its premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.
	

	“Who do you imagine yourself singing like if you could sing like somebody?” Penn told the packed theater. “This movie is the song I dreamed I could sing.”

	Penn was one of several Oscar winners at the 12th edition of Doc Stories that concluded on Sunday. 

	Anne Lai, SFFILM executive director, said the organization’s mission, embodied by Doc Stories and the annual San Francisco Film Festival, is to keep independent voices alive by supporting filmmakers with distinctive work and helping them reach audiences.

	“That means not only supporting films and filmmakers who are trying to put distinctive work out into the world, but also growing and sharing that work with audiences,” said Lai. “So as we talk about consolidations of studios and what happens on the margins, I think a lot about us as an organization is trying to look at what is in the margins because a lot of the most interesting things do not come through the mainstream.”

	Academy Award-winner Laura Poitras attended the fest with her short “They’re Here,” about ICE agents’ descent on Minneapolis. It was one of 11 short documentaries that screened at Doc Stories. 
	

	Poitras and “They’re Here” co-director Rachel Lauren Mueller spoke in depth about making the film during the fest’s Doc Talks series.

	“We describe (the film) as a horror documentary,” said Mueller, who is Minneapolis-based and shot most of the doc in January and February 2026 while residents were evading and resisting the paramilitary occupation of their city.

	“Being in the occupation just as a human being and not even as a filmmaker was one of the most difficult experiences of my life,” Mueller said. “There were tanks rolling down my street. It was not the first time. That also happened after the murder of George Floyd, but this was different because the streets were filled with tear gas. They were kidnapping people from street corners right around my house.”

	Poitras, known for her feature documentaries including “Citizenfour,” “All the Beauty and the Bloodshed” and “Cover-Up,” said that the gravity of the situation was one reason she and Mueller decided to make “They’re Here” a short film.

	“I’ve worked in short form and long form, and the truth is feature-length documentaries often take longer, and I think we both felt a sense of urgency of making something that could be released in a more contemporaneous moment,” said Poitras.

	“They’re Here” was one of several Oscar-qualified films that screened at Doc Stories. Others included Sam Pollard’s “Tutu,” J.M. Harper’s “Soul Patrol,” and Ava DuVernay‘s “14th.”

	DuVernay said the Democrats’ midterm victory could make “14th”  and its exploration of belonging and birthright citizenship even more resonant.

	“The film goes far beyond this moment,” said DuVernay. “This film is about the structural challenges that we have had as a country, and until you know the machinery of elections, they are not going to get us to where we need to be. So, this is the right time for people to get past the vote, vote, vote of it all and into the OK, this is how we actually make systemic change.”

	Doc Stories is considered an essential stop on the Oscar-season circuit because of its curation and the Bay Area’s concentration of AMPAS Documentary Branch and guild members. Its selections have a strong track record with the Academy. More than two dozen Doc Stories selections have earned Academy Award nominations, and several have won, including “No Other Land” and “Summer of Soul.”
	

	“The doc community here is very engaged, committed, and vibrant, and they show up for each other,” said Jessie Fairbanks, SFFILM’s director of programming. “They want to see each other’s work and talk about what they are working on.

	“There is usually some synergy just because of where we sit in the calendar year and the types of films that are campaigning, which is wonderful because it means we get a heightened profile for the festival. The doc community here is very engaged, committed, and vibrant, and they show up for each other. They want to see each other’s work and talk about what they are working on,” said Fairbanks.

	Like DOC NYC’s annual Visionaries Luncheon, Doc Stories’ annual brunch brings together the who’s who of the doc community and lets filmmakers, producers, editors, cinematographers, and publicists schmooze with branch members before the Oscar Short List voting deadline. DuVernay and Netflix’s doc VP Adam Del Deo flew in for the lunch, as did the filmmakers behind “To Hold a Mountain” and Frontline’s Raney Aronson-Rath, who is campaigning for “One in a Million.”

	Unlike for-profit DOC NYC, Doc Stories is a nonprofit festival, with a much smaller brunch than DOC NYC’s annual Visionaries Luncheon. 

	“Different organizations engage with the awards campaign in different ways,” said Fairbanks. “We don’t charge people a fee to be a part of our events. If you want access to the brunch, you can sponsor us, a nonprofit organization, and get access to the room; otherwise, you have to be a filmmaker who is a part of our organization, or you are an (AMPAS) voter. Monetizing that allows us to retain our independence when it comes to what we curate and what we put in front of audiences.”

schema.headline: Sean Penn, Ava DuVernay and Laura Poitras Turn Out For San Francisco’s Doc Stories

title: Bong Joon Ho on Restoring ‘The Host’ and Why It Still Resonates 20 Years On: ‘We Are Repeating Our Mistakes’
description: Bong Joon Ho has revisited “The Host” for a 20th-anniversary 4K restoration, and the Oscar-winning director says the 2006 monster movie’s satire of
body:
Bong Joon Ho has revisited “The Host” for a 20th-anniversary 4K restoration, and the Oscar-winning director says the 2006 monster movie’s satire of official misinformation feels newly pertinent.

	Magnolia Pictures will return the remastered film to theaters nationwide on Nov. 20. Screenings on Nov. 21 and 23 will include an exclusive conversation between Bong and filmmaker Edgar Wright.


	“I can’t believe it’s been 20 years since the release of the film. Time flies,” Bong tells Variety.
	

	In “The Host,” Song Kang-ho plays Gang-du, who nods off on the job at his snack kiosk beside Seoul’s Han River. A monstrous creature crawls out of the water, tears through the crowds on the riverbank and snatches his schoolgirl daughter Hyun-seo, played by Ko A-sung. Authorities declare the creature the carrier of an unknown virus. When Gang-du gets a phone call from Hyun-seo, terrified but alive, he resolves to slip into the sealed-off zone by the river and bring her back. Byun Hee-bong, Park Hae-il and Bae Doo-na co-star as members of his family. New Zealand’s Weta Workshop built detailed models of the creature, and The Orphanage handled visual effects and animation.

	Bong’s later film “Parasite” won the Palme d’Or in 2019 and went on to win four Oscars, including best picture, making it the first non-English-language film to take the top prize.

	Bong wrote “The Host” with the SARS outbreak in mind. A scene in which U.S. lawmakers concede there never was a virus spreading through Korea was his satire of the misinformation behind the Iraq War, launched over weapons of mass destruction that turned out not to exist. Since then, Bong notes, the world has lived through the coronavirus pandemic.
	

	“Now we’re in the thick of the Iran War and we’re still in the midst of an ongoing war, and whether it’s good history or bad history, it seems like we as a community, as a whole, are repeating our mistakes,” Bong says. “Although the film has stayed the same, the history is repeating itself and making the film relevant again.”

	The aim of the restoration, Bong says, was to recreate the experience of watching a fresh 35mm print, as the film was shown when it premiered at Cannes in 2006. “The Host” was shot on Fuji stock rather than Kodak, and Bong wanted to bring back the subtle color qualities he first worked out with his cinematographer Kim Hyung-ku during the shoot.

	“Ironically, we were using digital technology to enhance the film look of the movie,” Bong says.

	Because the effects work was done in 2005 and 2006, before 4K was available, those shots had to be upscaled. Bong says the team took care that the creature still blended convincingly with the actors and their surroundings, and he is satisfied with the result. He still spots minor flaws in the CGI when he watches the film now, along with parts that leave him slightly dissatisfied.

	“But I believe that the film is a record of what I was as a filmmaker at the time, and so I do not have any wishes to correct that,” Bong says. “Just like we don’t edit or rewrite our journals, I feel like it should just be left as it is.”

	Bong points to Ridley Scott, who removed a few shots when he re-released the original 1979 “Alien.”

	“I also had that kind of impulse, but luckily I was able to hold myself back,” Bong says. “It wasn’t a lot of shots. It was only one or two shots where I thought maybe I could cut that out, but in the end, I just resisted the impulse.”

	He declines to say which moment he had in mind, calling it a secret.

	Bong did the sound work on “The Host” at Livetone, the Seoul facility where he says he has worked with the same sound supervisor for 25 years, even as cinematographers and other crew members changed from film to film. The studio still holds the original sound library. His films from “Okja” onward, including “Parasite,” have been mixed in Dolby Atmos, and he says “The Host” could be upgraded to that format, though he still needs to confirm which sound format the North American release will use.
	

	The creature’s voice was the area of the original sound design he concentrated on most. The team recorded and processed the sounds of a sea lion, then layered in a vocal performance from Korean actor Oh Dal-su, mixing the two into the sound audiences heard in theaters.

	Bong sees little point in remastering his later work, since everything after “Okja” was shot in 4K and finished with Atmos sound. He has, however, made black-and-white versions of “Mother” and “Parasite,” screening them in small theatrical releases and at festivals.

	“I have great admiration for black-and-white films,” Bong says. “It’s a process that I enjoyed very much.”

	Bong had previously told Variety that after his animated feature “Ally,” he would turn to a slate of crime and horror films. Asked whether that is still the plan, he confirms it.

	“I want to return home,” Bong says.

schema.headline: Bong Joon Ho on Restoring ‘The Host’ and Why It Still Resonates 20 Years On: ‘We Are Repeating Our Mistakes’

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Superfans Hit Theaters for Shane and Ilya on the Big Screen: ‘They Invented Chemistry’
description: A sea of women and a scattering of men packed into the Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria Sunday night for a cinematic experience. Not to see a new movie,
body:
A sea of women and a scattering of men packed into the Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria Sunday night for a cinematic experience. Not to see a new movie, but to celebrate the one-year anniversary of the hit HBO Max-Crave series “Heated Rivalry.”

	Based on Rachel Reid’s bestselling “Game Changers” books and adapted by Jacob Tierney, the queer hockey romance-turned global phenomenon follows the illicit and decades-spanning relationship between two rival hockey stars, Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie).
	

	As fans eagerly await Season 2, which is currently in production, Season 1 was released in theaters, inviting audiences to watch the love story unfold on the big screen for the first time.

	Some loyalists donned their best Boston Raiders or Montreal Metros T-shirts, others filled their special edition popcorn buckets and soda cups, but all erupted into raucous cheers while viewing the penultimate and final episodes of the first season. Variety spoke with a few of these “Heated Rivalry” enthusiasts to discuss the appeal of the theater experience and hear what makes the series so special to them.

	“Look at them, they’re hot!” Crystal Naldi, 32, said gesturing to her popcorn bucket emblazoned with the show’s poster art. “No, I’m playing. I honestly wasn’t into the show at first, but my friends kept nagging at me to watch it. I really wanted to see this because I didn’t get to see ‘Red, White and Royal Blue’ on screen. I was like, ‘I know I’m gonna kick my own ass if I don’t go to the theater. I better fucking go.’”
	

	“I’m down to financially support the show’s success, and also both Hudson and Connor’s success as actors,” Aubrie Shadday, 29, said.

	“Seeing it on the big screen with people is so fun, and having the live reaction because everyone watched it essentially by themselves, so hearing everyone giggle or laugh or sniffle here and there is really cool,” Yesenia Vargas, 28, added.

	Fans admitted that they had already seen the series several times, but the silver screen revealed or amplified details they glossed over during their first viewing.

	“I’m getting goose bumps over scenes I’ve seen 30 times,” Anna, 44, said. “You can hear things you didn’t hear before, like Ilya’s necklace during certain scenes and see Hudson’s watery eyeballs this big.”

	“Something about seeing it on the big screen is just insane,” Sam, 34, chimed in. “I do think this is how I need to watch everything I like a lot.”

	Fans also rejoiced over Williams and Storrie’s undeniable connection, attributing their magnetism to the show’s widespread appeal.

	“I’ve never seen that seemingly realistic chemistry before, and now I feel like I can’t watch anything else, romance-wise, because I’m like ‘this is fake,’” Shadday said. “I don’t know how they did it. They’re very talented, but it just hits. I like romance in general, but I feel like this hits a lot more than other shows just because their chemistry is so realistic.”

	“It made me hopeful for romance,” Taylor Benson, 37, said.

	“I don’t think we’ve seen a true love story like this, a queer love story, the diversity of it is really cool,” Vargas said.

	“It’s just the greatest love story ever told,” Anna said. “A lot of people make lowbrow jokes like ‘Oh, gay and sexy.’ It’s so much more than that. It’s seeing these two people fall in love and their relationship develop, and the chemistry is unlike chemistry I’ve seen between two actors.”

	“I’m pretty sure they invented chemistry,” Sam added. “I’m positive that it didn’t exist before them.”

	Another big draw for fans was hearing the powerful soundtrack and pulsing score boom through the theater’s speakers.

	“I think that Jacob did a really great job. He made it a beautiful show, and I used to work in post-production music and the music is amazing,” Benson said.
	

	“I also really like the score and the music,” Vargas said. “I feel like I always watch things and always pay attention to what songs or how the score sounds, and seeing that obviously now on a bigger screen with an amazing sound system helps tell the story.”

	Many of these superfans also retroactively read the books. Since they already know the plot of Season 2, they’re mostly looking forward to seeing their favorite couple back in love.

	“I’m just looking forward to the fact that it’s coming,” Benson said.

	“Them just being together as a united front, even though it’s still in secret, is definitely what I’m looking forward to,” Naldi said.

	“I’m excited to see Connor and Hudson get even more into the thick of it emotionally,” Shadday said, with Anna adding “Just the continuation of their love story and being able to see queer joy continue to be explored and to be able to see them living their truth.”

title: Tom Brady and Jim Harbaugh Exec Produce ‘The Team: Michigan Football,’ Set to Debut on Fox This Month (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Fox Sports has greenlighted the two-part documentary “The Team: Michigan Football,” which centers on Michigan’s college football program and its tw
body:
Fox Sports has greenlighted the two-part documentary “The Team: Michigan Football,” which centers on Michigan’s college football program and its two championship eras. Shadow Lion is behind the series, which is also executive produced by Tom Brady and Jim Harbaugh. The two-part series premieres on Friday, Nov. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on Fox — the eve of Michigan’s game vs. Ohio State, which takes place the next day. Part 2 of “The Team: Michigan Football” will air Saturday, Dec. 12, at 6:30 p.m. ET on Fox.
	

	Here’s the logline: “Featuring never-before-seen footage and firsthand accounts from Michigan greats including Fox NFL lead analyst and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady, legendary coach Jim Harbaugh, Pro Football Hall of Famer and ‘Fox NFL Kickoff’ analyst Charles Woodson, famed quarterback J.J. McCarthy, three-time national championship-winning head coach and ‘Fox Big Noon Kickoff’ analyst Urban Meyer, NFL stars Blake Corum and Brian Griese and other renowned sports figures, ‘The Team: Michigan Football’ takes viewers inside Michigan’s historic 1997 and 2023 national championship seasons to examine the tradition, expectations and intense scrutiny that shaped both teams, revealing what it takes to compete at the highest level while navigating the tension between individual ambition and the demands of putting the team first.”

	Said Brady in a statement: “Thinking about my years at Michigan brings up a lot of emotions because, like many of my teammates, it really shaped who I became as a player and person. I’m excited to share that story alongside the personal experiences of so many others who were transformed by this historic program, and I couldn’t have asked for better partners to do it with than Fox Sports and Shadow Lion.”
	

	Part one, “The Eye of the Storm,” centers on Harbaugh’s relationship to the Michigan football program, including as a player and then leading the team to the 2023 national championship as head coach. Part two, “Those Who Stay,” centers on the team’s 1990s run, including its journey to the 1997 national championship and Brady’s rise as a player.

	“It’s been an honor to help tell this story and shed new light on one of the most iconic programs in sports,” said Shadow Lion’s Jeff Fine, director and executive producer, in a statement. “I’m incredibly grateful to the talented team who brought the ‘Those Who Stay Will Be Champions’ mentality to every step of the filmmaking process.”

	Added Fox Sports president and exec producer Brad Zager in a statement: “There’s no better team to partner with than Tom Brady, Coach Harbaugh and Shadow Lion to bring Michigan’s championship history to life. Tom and Jim’s deep ties to the program bring a unique perspective to this documentary, giving viewers an inside look at two defining championship eras in Ann Arbor.”

	Shadpw Lion produces “The Team: Michigan Football.” Fine is director, while Dexton Deboree is co-director. Executive producers include Tom Brady, Jim Harbaugh, Gilad Haas, Jeff Fine, Lior Haas, Philip Byron, Steve Dubin, Dexton Deboree and Jordan Savage. Michael Lucks, Trevor MacKinnon and Alex Sandman are co-executive producers.

title: XYZ Films, CAA Media Finance Ink U.S. Deal With Samuel Goldwyn Films for Dark Comedy ‘Kill Me’ Starring Charlie Day and Allison Williams (EXCLUSIVE)
description: XYZ Films and CAA Media Finance inked a deal with Samuel Goldwyn Films for U.S. rights to “Kill Me,” a murder mystery comedy film from writer-direc
body:
XYZ Films and CAA Media Finance inked a deal with Samuel Goldwyn Films for U.S. rights to “Kill Me,” a murder mystery comedy film from writer-director Peter Warren starring Charlie Day and Allison Williams. A theatrical release is planned for Spring 2027. 

	The official logline for “Kill Me” reads, “Jimmy (Day) didn’t try to kill himself. Or at least, he’s pretty sure he didn’t. With the help of a reluctant 911 operator (Williams), he sets out on an amateur investigation to solve the ultimate mystery: is he being stalked by a killer, or chasing himself?” Other cast members include Giancarlo Esposito, Aya Cash, Jessica Harper, David Krumholtz and Tony Cavalero.
	

	“We’re thrilled to partner with Samuel Goldwyn Films to bring ‘Kill Me’ to US audiences,” XYZ Films said in a statement. “Peter expertly blends dark comedy, mystery and suspense with terrific performances from Charlie, Allison and the entire cast.”

	Producers for “Kill Me” include Day, Maxime Cottray for XYZ Films, Nate Bolotin, Keith Goldberg, Mike Richardson, Natalie Metzger for Vanishing Angle and Warren. Williams, Esposito, Paul Schwake, Kasey Adler, Vanishing Angle’s Matt Miller, Timo Argillander and IPR.VC’s Andrea Scarso serve as executive producers.

	“Charlie Day and Alison Williams deliver performances that are funny, surprising and moving and director Peter Warren has made a dark comedy with real heart. We’re thrilled to be partnering with XYZ Films to bring ‘Kill Me’ to audiences across the country.” said Peter Goldwyn, president of Samuel Goldwyn Films.
	

	Day is best known for his work on FX’s long-running, raunchy sitcom “It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia,” which launched its 18th season in August. On the big screen, his recent credits include “Wildwood,” “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and “Honey Don’t!” Williams broke out starring in HBO’s coming-of-age drama series “Girls,” which is getting the reboot treatment in 2027. Her recent movie credits include “Regretting You” and “M3GAN 2.0.” Coming up, she has the sci-fi thriller “Homewrecker” with Michelle Randolph and “Tangled Up in Blue” from Jamie Adams.

	The deal was negotiated by Pip Ngo of XYZ Films, alongside CAA Media Finance, on behalf of the filmmakers and by Goldwyn for Samuel Goldwyn Films.

schema.headline: XYZ Films, CAA Media Finance Ink U.S. Deal With Samuel Goldwyn Films for Dark Comedy ‘Kill Me’ Starring Charlie Day and Allison Williams (EXCLUSIVE)

title: DC in Flux: What Happens to James Gunn’s Batman, Superman and Other Heroes After Shocking Exit?
description:
Nov 9, 2026 2:13pm PT	
	

	
		DC in Flux: What Happens to James Gunn’s Batman, Superman and Other Heroes After Shocking Exit?
body:
Nov 9, 2026 2:13pm PT	
	

	
		DC in Flux: What Happens to James Gunn’s Batman, Superman and Other Heroes After Shocking Exit?
	
	
			


			
			
	

	

		
	
				

	James Gunn and Peter Safran are out as the CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios, leaving behind a cinematic universe full of questions about the fate of some of Hollywood’s most beloved and profitable heroes.

	After four years at the helm, it seemed like Gunn and Safran had just set the foundation for things to come at DC. Audiences got the first taste of DCU 2.0 with 2025’s “Superman.” David Corenswet starred as the titular Man of Steel, and Nicholas Hoult was second billed as supervillain Lex Luthor. The film was a relative success, earning $618 million at the worldwide box office. Their next film, “Supergirl,” didn’t perform nearly as well, bombing with $126 million against a $170 million budget. The duo’s final big-screen bout, “Clayface,” hit theaters in late October and pulled in $109 million from a $44 million budget. On the small screen “Peacemaker” and “Lanterns” on HBO helped fill in the gaps between the films with some early hints of franchise interconnectivity.

	Outside of what made it on screen, there was plenty of talk about projects in the works. Gunn recently teased that he is searching for his own DCU Batman, separate from Matt Reeves’ work with the character. There was also recent talk about bringing Margot Robbie back as Harley Quinn. Projects like “Swamp Thing,” from James Mangold, and the long-rumored “Wonder Woman” movie also remain in varying stages of development. What we do know is that Gunn and Safran will close out their remaining creative commitments with DC Studios. Those commitments most notably include the “Superman” sequel, “Man of Tomorrow,” which wrapped in late August. It brings back original stars like Corenswet, Hoult, Rachel Brosnahan and Skyler Gisondo and welcomes newcomers like Lars Eidinger as Brainiac and Adria Arjona as Maxima (though rumors swirl that she’s actually playing Wonder Woman).

	Without much concrete continuity in place, Marvel vet Jeremy Latcham, who produced superhero tentpoles like “Iron Man,” “The Avengers” and “Spider-Man: Homecoming,” among others, can take DC wherever he pleases. Will franchise stars like Corenswet stay on board, or will Latcham clean house to make room for a new vision?

	After Gunn and Safran’s exit, Variety created a list of some of DC’s biggest names and compiled all the info that could point to their future under Latcham’s rule.


			
			
			
										
					Image Credit: Everett Collection				
					
				
	David Corenswet will don his Superman cape and trunks in next summer’s sequel “Man of Tomorrow,” written and directed by Gunn. The new Man of Steel headlined Gunn and Safran’s reboot of the DC Universe and turned out to be a moderate box office hit. It seems likely that Latcham would keep Corenswet in the role, considering Superman was essentially the face of the new universe and one of DC’s crown jewels. Cornswet’s take on the hero was warmly welcomed by fans, as was Nicholas Hoult as his nemesis Lex Luthor. The two will pair up to take down the evil alien genius Brainiac in “Man of Tomorrow,” alongside several of the “Superman” supporting cast. Now fans will just have to wait patiently until Superman can team up with DC’s other major stars, Batman and Wonder Woman.
		
			
			
	Batman
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	Batman is DC’s most popular — and lucrative — character, but his future is almost as murky as the shadows he creeps in. Robert Pattinson starred in Matt Reeves’ blockbuster “Batman” movie, which grossed $772.8 million globally. Excitement for Reeves and Pattinson’s sequel has been high, but it’s been beset by several delays. “The Batman: Part II” is slated to release Feb. 18, 2028, but Reeves had to step away from production due to a family matter; Steven Soderbergh then stepped in to help finish the shoot.

	However, Pattinson’s Caped Crusader predated Gunn and Safran’s DC tenure and is completely separate from their universe. Reeves has spoken about having plans for a Batman trilogy, but now it’s unclear whether it would continue under new leadership. Gunn also planned to cast a new Batman in the rebooted DC Universe in a “Brave and the Bold” movie that would inhabit the same world as Corenswet’s Superman. Fans have long called for Pattinson to cross over into the main DCU, but would he stick firmly in Reeves’ universe and then hang up the cowl? His gritty take on the hero may be at odds in the Gunn-created world, but stranger things have happened in comic book movies.

		
			
			
	Wonder Woman
			
										
					Image Credit: Clay Enos / © Warner Bros. / Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Part of DC’s Big Three superheroes, Wonder Woman has been absent from the DC Universe since 2020’s poorly received “Wonder Woman 1984,” starring Gal Gadot. The love for the character is there, considering Gadot’s first movie made a whopping $823 million globally, but there haven’t been any concrete plans to reintroduce the Amazon hero to the DCU. Gunn had slated a “Paradise Lost” TV series about Wonder Woman’s early days at HBO, but it was officially scrapped this summer. There are also rumors that Adria Arjona may secretly debut as the character in next year’s “Man of Tomorrow,” but she could also just be playing an alien warrior queen named Maxima from the “Superman” mythos. Arjona’s star has been on the rise since breaking out in “Andor,” “Hit Man” and next year’s “The Thomas Crown Affair,” and it might be an easy win for DC to introduce her as Wonder Woman then put her in a standalone movie — if the rumors are true.
		
			
			
	Justice League
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Warner Bros.				
					
				
	“Superman” introduced the Justice Gang, a rough-draft version of the Justice League that included the Man of Steel, Mister Terrific (Edi Gathegi), Hawkgirl (Isabela Merced), Metamorpho (Anthony Carrigan) and Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion). “Man of Tomorrow” will look to bolster the ranks with characters like Supergirl, John Stewart, Blue Beetle and maybe even Wonder Woman. That seems like a solid start for the Justice League, but it lacks the traditional founding members like Aquaman, Flash and Cyborg (who all starred in Zack Snyder’s “Justice League” movie). The DCU can set itself apart with its fresh team of heroes, but no Justice League can be complete without Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman. Without the latter two heroes cast in the universe, don’t count on seeing a standalone “Justice League” movie for a few years.
		
			
			
	Green Lantern
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of HBO				
					
				
	The Green Lanterns made a major comeback in Gunn’s universe, with Nathan Fillion playing Guy Gardner in “Superman” and Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler’s “Lanterns” HBO series. They played John Stewart and Hal Jordan, two of the most famous members of the intergalactic Green Lantern Corps, and Pierre will reprise the role in “Man of Tomorrow.” “Lanterns” was a decent ratings hit for HBO, but a Season 2 renewal hasn’t been announced. With the leadership changes and a bigger budget needed for sophomore season, the Green Lanterns’ light may be dimming for now.
		
			
			
	Supergirl
			
										
					Image Credit: Warner Bros.				
					
				
	After the success of last year’s “Superman,” all eyes were on “Supergirl” to begin a box-office hot streak for the DCU, but it went cold. The movie, starring Milly Alcock as Superman’s cousin, only made $126 million, a major flop. She’ll return in “Man of Tomorrow,” but it would be surprising if Supergirl takes flight again in a solo movie.
		
			
			
	Clayface
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Released just last month, “Clayface” has been a low-budget success and proved that not all superhero movies have to cost hundreds of millions of dollars. Starring Tom Rhys Harries as a shape-shifting monster, “Clayface” was planned as a standalone villain movie without any Batman connections, so don’t expect to see him to take shape in another DC film.
		
			
			
	Harley Quinn
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Margot Robbie’s Harley Quinn was the lone bright spot of the 2016 “Suicide Squad” movie, and she popped back in for “Birds of Prey” and Gunn’s 2021 “The Suicide Squad.” She hasn’t reprised her role since, but DC fans loved her take on the Joker’s chaotic partner. Robbie may be retired from playing Harley, but it might be an easy win for the DCU to bring her back à la Hugh Jackman in “Deadpool & Wolverine.”
		
			
			
	Blue Beetle
			
								
				
	“Blue Beetle” had the bad luck of releasing during the actors strike, so the cast and star Xolo Maridueña didn’t do much press for the movie — and it underperformed at the box office with $130 million. In a surprise move, though, Maridueña is returning for “Man of Tomorrow,” but it seems far-fetched that he’d suit up again in another movie.
		
			
			
	Peacemaker
			
										
					Image Credit: Max				
					
				
	Gunn created “Peacemaker,” starring John Cena as his violently patriotic “Suicide Squad” character, before he took over DC Studios. The show debuted on HBO in 2022, and the second season arrived four years later after on HBO in the wake of “Superman.” The show’s future is unclear: It was never renewed for Season 3, but it was also never canceled. Without Gunn at DC, though, “Peacemaker” will probably not return.
		
			
			
	Creature Commandos
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of DC Studios				
					
				
	Gunn’s “Creature Commandos” animated series was the first official project in the new DCU when it dropped on HBO in December 2024, and it was renewed for Season 2. The follow-up season is expected to air next year after “Man of Tomorrow” hits theaters, but a potential Season 3 seems tough with Gunn’s exit.
		
			
			
	Swamp Thing, Bane, Deathstroke and More
			
										
					Image Credit: Warner Bros.				
					
				
	Several other DC movies were announced during Gunn and Safran’s tenure, but no official greenlights or many other details were ever set. Director James Mangold was attached to a Swamp Thing movie, while other projects on Batman villains like Bane and Deathstroke and the Teen Titans team were in the works. With a new leader and vision for the DCU, the status of every unconfirmed project is up in the air, but without a clear slate it seems unlikely they’ll come to fruition.
		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

title: Skydance Q3 Profit Powered By Studios, Streaming
description: Skydance, fresh from completing its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, said the Paramount part of the business generated profit of $73 million — a
body:
Skydance, fresh from completing its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, said the Paramount part of the business generated profit of $73 million — a swing from a loss in the year-earlier period — but the results did not include data from its new properties, because its deal did not close until October, after the fiscal period had ended.

	The owner of CBS, CNN and the Paramount and Warner Bros. movie studios said net income came to six cents per share, and to 45 cents per share when adjusted for pretax expenses and non-recurring costs.
	

	The company said revenue of $7.03 billion in the period, an increase of 5% over the year-earlier quarter. 

	Revenue fell at Skydance’s largest operation, its traditional TV division, down 7% to $3 billion. Advertising revenue fell 8%, due in part to the sale of Telefe and Chilevisión in October 2025 and January 2026, respectively. Distribution revenue fell 5% due to continued  subscriber erosion.

	Revenue from direct to consumer operations rose 11% to $2.5 billion, with the company citing accelerating Paramount+ revenue growth of 21% year-over-year, and subscriber growth of approximately 6%.

	Revenue from studios rose 23% to $1.5 billion, due in large part to licensing and content produced for third parties.

	In a letter to shareholders, the company said the Warner Bros. studio was not performing as well as the one at Paramount.  “We expect the Warner Bros. film slate in Q4 to underperform,” the company said, while noting that “Paramount Pictures continues to perform well and is expected to double its output in 2026 with 15 releases.”
	

	The company also indicated it expected to be able to both cut costs and to invest for the future. Skydance continues to “expect to achieve at least $6 billion in run-rate synergies, net of reinvestment across our cost structure within three years.” And executives said they believe that “by combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion.

	Skydance also disclosed that it will follow the lead of Netflix, Disney and other major streamers by ending its quarterly reporting of streaming subscribers as of its Q4 report to come early next year. At present, Paramount+ and HBO Max combined account for some 203 million global subscribers.

	In the shareholder letter penned by David Ellison, Skydance chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, co-CEO, the two touted Skydance’s “industry-leading” budget for content spending, which has topped $30 billion. 

	“We also see opportunity in content, which is both an expense for us but also an investment in building valuable, long-term assets for the company,” Ellison and Kreiz wrote. “We start from an industry-leading base of more than $30 billion in annual content spend and a deep library built over a combined 200-plus years of storytelling, and we will keep investing in the content engine that drives our growth. With the reach of our combined platforms across streaming, broadcast and cable, each title can work harder for us, and as one company we can make smarter choices about how we distribute and monetize our slate.”

title: Skydance Plans Launch of Bundled Paramount+, HBO Max in Early 2027
description: Streaming fans will soon be able to subscribe to a new bundled service that offers access to”Tulsa King” and “The White Lotus” for a single price.
body:
Streaming fans will soon be able to subscribe to a new bundled service that offers access to”Tulsa King” and “The White Lotus” for a single price.

	Skydance, in one of its first big announcement since completing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, said it planned to launch Paramount+ and HBO Max as part of a single offer as soon as early 2027.

	‘Starting in early 2027, consumers will be able to subscribe to both world-class streaming services at an even greater value,” the company said Monday in a letter to shareholders. “We look forward to sharing more details on the bundle and our streaming roadmap in the coming months.” 
	

	The piecing together of two services with disparate programming themes — HBO Max has a reputation for drawing fans of premium storytelling on the order of “House of Dragons” or “Lanterns,” while Paramount+ has a more meat-and-potatoes demeanor highlighted by the “Yellowstone” suite of dramas and the CBS programming schedule — is seen as a key maneuver to make the company more competitive with offerings like Netflix, Disney+, or Amazon’s Prime Video.

	HBO Max features talk-show programming from Bill Maher and John Oliver, popular dramas including “Game of Thrones” and “The Sopranos” and recent phenoms like “Eurphoria.” Paramount+ includes programming tied to CBS, Nickelodeon and Comedy Central as well as originals such as “Landman,” “Lioness” and a suite of series tied to the company’s “Star Trek” franchise.

	Skydance CEO David Ellison suggested the bundle would stand as a “first step” toward creating a combined service over a longer time frame. During a call with investors, Ellison said the two services are complementary and index heavily with different sets of subscribers across the U.S.
	

	Skydance did not say if it would end other bundles that use the properties. HBO Max has for some time been offered with a bundle that includes Disney streamers Disney+ and Hulu. During the investor call, Ellison suggested the company would examine such arrangements to determine if they drove sharehodler value.

schema.headline: Skydance Plans Launch of Bundled Paramount+, HBO Max in Early 2027

title: AMC Global Media Takes $2.1 Million Hit Amid ALLBLK Streamer Sale, Content Licensing Revenue Up 42% in Q3
description: AMC Global Media reported its third-quarter 2026 earnings Monday, revealing a major increase in content licensing sales and a restructuring charge
body:
AMC Global Media reported its third-quarter 2026 earnings Monday, revealing a major increase in content licensing sales and a restructuring charge of $2.1 million following the sale of its ALLBLK streaming service.

	Additionally, AMC says its Sept. 4 settlement agreement with “The Walking Dead” creator Robert Kirkman and other series producers led to a cash payment of $85 million with $35 million still left to be paid no later than Jan. 31, 2027. As a result of the lawsuit’s outcome, AMC recorded a charge of $85 million in consideration for the dismissal of the action with prejudice during the July-Sept. quarter. 
	

	Wall Street forecast a loss of earnings per share (EPS) of 1 cent on $584.9 million in revenue, according to analyst consensus data provided by LSEG. AMC reported adjusted EPS of 44 cents on $566 million in revenue.

	“We saw consolidated revenue growth in the third quarter, led by our licensing and streaming businesses,” AMC Global Media CEO Kristin Dolan said in a letter to shareholders. “We also saw sequential and year-over-year improvements in both domestic affiliate and advertising revenue trends. We continue to leverage our key points of differentiation including a targeted streaming strategy that is complementary to larger and more expensive options from other providers, running on a single technology platform with attractive pricing and packaging. Our AMC Studios business is creating valuable and distinctive IP for our own platforms and for partners through co-production relationships and content sales.”

title: ‘GTA 6’ Presales ‘Far in Excess’ of Expectations Ahead of Next Week’s Launch, Take-Two CEO Says
description: Rockstar Games‘ “Grand Theft Auto VI” presales are “running far in excess of our expectations,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said Monda
body:
Rockstar Games‘ “Grand Theft Auto VI” presales are “running far in excess of our expectations,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said Monday. 

	“That’s a good thing. That said, we never claim success before it occurs,” Zelnick told Variety in an interview ahead of the company’s earnings release. “So we’re just days away from from beginning to see the fruits of our labor.”

	“GTA 6” will launch Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S and X devices priced at $79.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the ultimate version. While Rockstar has yet to confirm exact pre-order results for the title, despite some rumors floating around regarding sales, Zelnick assures the company will “certainly be giving more information about how ‘GTA 6’ performs post-launch.”
	

	The results are in line with what Zelnick and Rockstar previously disclosed after pre-orders began in June and reached “unprecedented” levels at that time. 

	On Monday, SAG-AFTRA released a statement in support of Rockstar Games workers’ decision to unionize, which Zelnick declined to comment on when speaking with Variety.

	As for if and when “GTA 6” will make it onto other platforms, like PC and Nintendo Switch 2, or see a full physical disc release, Zelnick says that “information always comes from our labels” and will leave those potential future announcements to Rockstar.

	Take-Two’s game revenue for the July-Sept. quarter was $1.38 billion. Ad sales reached $121 million. Sales for “NBA 2K” were softer than anticipated.

	Wall Street forecast a loss of earnings per share (EPS) of 86 cents on $1.66 billion in revenue, according to analyst consensus data provided by LSEG. Take-Two Interactive reported a loss per share of 29 cents and net bookings of $1.6 billion. The company reported a loss of $54 million for the quarter.

schema.headline: ‘GTA 6’ Presales ‘Far in Excess’ of Expectations Ahead of Next Week’s Launch, Take-Two CEO Says

title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard Avoids Family Drama at Ken Urker's Memorial Service
description:
Gypsy Rose Blanchard
                          Dodges Ken Urker's Sis at His Memorial
body:
Gypsy Rose Blanchard
                          Dodges Ken Urker's Sis at His Memorial
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 9, 2026
                            11:30 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 9, 2026
                                12:38 PM PST
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Gypsy Rose Blanchard came to honor her baby daddy, Ken Urker, not reignite a family feud ... and she left his memorial shortly after his sister showed up.
      
    
            Family sources tell TMZ ... Ken's Celebration of Life was held Saturday at a venue in Austin, Texas ... with about 30 of his closest friends and relatives gathering to remember him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We're told Gypsy attended with their daughter, Aurora, and her stepmother, Kristy ... and even delivered a speech during the service, which also featured a slideshow honoring Ken.
      

            But things got interesting toward the end ... sources say Gypsy stepped away to change Aurora's diaper, and when she returned, she spotted Ken's sister Autumn, who has publicly criticized Gypsy in the past.
      
    
            Rather than risk an awkward encounter, we're told Gypsy informed Ken's family she was heading out ... and they were fine with it. The two women never crossed paths or spoke, and Gypsy joined Ken's family for breakfast the following morning.
      
    
            Sources add Autumn showed up with two friends who were turned away at the door ... because the family wanted to keep the gathering limited to people they knew.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Gypsy and Autumn's feud exploded after Ken's death, with Autumn accusing Gypsy of lying about her brother and Gypsy firing back that Autumn was disrespecting his memory. Gypsy even claimed the siblings weren't close and that Autumn had criticized Ken before his death.
      
    
            Gypsy also previously attended a private viewing for Ken in Louisiana with several of his relatives ... though Autumn was notably absent from that gathering.
      
    
            We broke the story ... Ken died October 1, on what would have been his 34th birthday, after being found unresponsive at his Louisiana home.
